# AinurLindalë {🗡️} {🎭🎴📜}

## Part 1 of 2

AinurLindalë is a world of rival realms and mixed bloodlines, connected by trade roads, border forts, and old promises that still bite. The Known World is what the mapmakers keep in ink: the crownlands of humankind, the deep canopy courts of the long-lived forestborn, the hidden groves of the fae, and the sun-baked dominions of the foxfolk. Yet no realm is a sealed jar—markets and ports are full of outsiders, settlers, deserters, pilgrims, and hired steel, so a banner never means only one face.

Step past the last milestone and the parchment turns cautious. Whole stretches remain uncharted: storm-cut valleys, drowned lowlands, forests where trails don't stay put. Ruins dot the wild like broken teeth—collapsed watchtowers, ivy-choked manors, half-buried gates, stairwells into black stone. Some belonged to old dynasties; others don't match any known craft, as if built by hands that played by different rules.

Magic is everywhere, practical in the cities and cruel in the dark. Wards keep streets safe; deeper out, traps don't rust, curses cling to flooded shrines, and relics feel warm when they shouldn't. Beasts roam the gaps between kingdoms, and stranger things—warped hybrids no bestiary agrees on—claim the places where maps go blank.

And beneath it all lie the dungeons: buried keeps, lost halls, vaults with locks too clean for their age, corridors lined with mechanisms still waiting. Push deep enough and you can come back with coin, steel, and wonders that change your fate—assuming you come back at all.

Now, in AinurLindalë, your story begins.
You are Zack, a 24-year-old Human. You are a Necromancer. You only just arrived to Silverhold when you see You're hit with a cliche scenario you'd expect of an anime, hit by a truck now you're opening your eyes in a new world



The cobblestones are cold under your back. You're staring up at a patch of gray sky framed by timbered overhangs and a dangling sign that creaks—The Rusty Flagon.

A sharp ache pulses in your ribs. You push yourself up onto your elbows, blinking. The world swims for a second, then snaps into focus.

You're in an alleyway, narrow and slick with runoff. The smell is a mix of wet stone, dung, and something sweet—baking bread from somewhere close.



 You don't know what's really going on but you chose a class and race so you assume this is some kind of video game world and you're ready for it. Necromancer? That should be a unique way to live in this new world.
You look around for where to begin this journey, an adventures guild? Something?

 You sit up fully, wincing at the soreness in your side. No truck. No asphalt. Just these worn cobbles and the damp chill seeping through your clothes. You're wearing simple, sturdy traveler's garb; linen shirt, wool trousers, a worn leather vest. A small pack lies beside you.

Across the alley, a door bangs open. A stout woman in an apron dumps a bucket of slops into the gutter, gives you a brief, disinterested glance, and retreats inside.



You get to your feet, brushing grit from your trousers. The alley opens onto a wider street; Lantern Row, according to a painted wooden sign nailed to a post. The air here is thicker, warmer, buzzing with voices and the clatter of carts. The buildings lean close, their upper stories jutting out, washing lines strung between them like festive bunting for rags.



You stand at the mouth of Lantern Row, the city's pulse thrumming around you. Hawkers shout over the rumble of cart wheels. The scent of roasting nuts and spilled ale mixes with the sharper tang of horse sweat and wet wool.

Ahead, a two-story building with a freshly painted sign—a shield crossed with a sword—hangs above a heavy oak door. Carved into the lintel are the words: The Gilded Gauntlet.



**You do**

> You should be a decent place to start, if it's not the right place to be it may have somebody who can point you the right way, you head for it.


You push open the heavy oak door of The Gilded Gauntlet and step inside.

The noise of Lantern Row fades, replaced by a low, steady hum of conversation and the clink of tankards. The common room is wide and timber-beamed, lit by iron lanterns hanging from hooks. A long bar of dark wood runs along one wall, behind which a bald, thick-armed man polishes a mug with a rag. Round tables are scattered across the floor, about half occupied.



**You do**

> You look for the right person to begin asking questions.


The room's eyes don't linger on you long; just another traveler, maybe a bit paler and thinner than most. You scan the faces. A group of three in leathers and cloaks, their heads bent close over a map, speak in low, urgent tones. Two older men in chain shirts argue quietly over a dice game. A woman in a green hood sits alone by the fire, nursing an ale and staring into the flames.

Behind the bar, the bald man catches your look.



The barkeep sets the mug down and leans his thick forearms on the bar. His eyes are a pale, assessing gray. "First time in Silverhold?"

His voice is a low rumble, carrying easily over the room's murmur. He doesn't smile, but his expression isn't unfriendly; more like a man taking stock of inventory.

"You look like you've just seen the cart that ran you over," he says, a dry note in his voice. "Ale? Or answers?"



**You say**

> You say, "Pretty sure I'm flat broke sorry to disappoint but I could really use a couple answers if you could"

"Name's Kael," he says, picking up the rag again and wiping the already-clean bar. "So. You're here. Woke up in an alley, I'm guessing."

"Alright," he says, lowering his voice a notch. "You want a start? There's the Chapterhall. Adventurer's Guild. Down in Rivergate Ward, near the docks. Big stone building with a bronze shield over the door. They have a board, contracts, rank seals."

"Lantern Row runs east-west. Head east until you hit the river. Turn right, follow the water. You'll see the Chapterhall. Can't miss it."

He picks up the rag again, his attention already drifting back to the mugs. The conversation is clearly over.

King Edric and Queen Lyra stand at the head of a long, polished table. But they are not alone.

**You say**

> You say, "Ah so that's the situation, how far into this discussion are we? Should I take place in this conversation or would you prefer I simply wait a moment for this business to be finished {the king before you left said he'd be replacing this man with Lord Garvin, the old treasurer before this man took over and began taking bribes}"


King Edric's jaw tightens. He shares a quick, loaded glance with Lyra. The Queen's expression is one of sharp, controlled focus.

Lord Vance's eyes narrow almost imperceptibly. He does not sit back down.

"We are discussing the state of the royal coffers," the King says, his voice carefully neutral. "And the... irregularities... discovered in recent transactions."



Lord Vance's gaze shifts from Edric to you. There is a cold calculation in his eyes, the kind of look a banker gives a ledger that doesn't balance.

"Irregularities," he repeats, the word smooth as oiled silk. "A curious term for a matter of state finance. I was just explaining to Their Majesties that the... sudden cessation of tribute payments to Lord Thorne's interests has created a significant... gap in the kingdom's projected outlays."



This man is discussing the slave trade like it was standard business or taxes for the kingdom, and he's ignoring the direct small fortune amassed by seizing Thorne's assets, you're genuinely curious as to how this will play out.

 The Queen's gaze is ice. "A gap, Lord Vance? You speak as if we misplaced a purse. These were bribes. Payments to a slaver."

Lord Vance spreads his hands, a gesture of practiced reason. "Your Majesty, I speak only of the ledgers. The Crown's commitments—treaties, garrisons, supply lines—were balanced against certain... predictable inflows. Removing them without a phased plan risks instability."



He's genuinely proposing that the lack of slavery and bribes is a problem. Very directly, it's almost funny if it wasn't so corrupt and disgusting.

 The Master of Coin's words hang in the air, a testament to the rot you've been ripping out by the roots. He's not defending Thorne, not exactly. He's defending the system that allowed Thorne to exist.

You step further into the room, letting the heavy door swing shut behind Finn, Eira, and Rylan.



**You say**

> You say, "Your majesties may I cut this discussion short? It seems rather counter productive when we have important matters to discuss."


Queen Lyra's eyes cut to you, sharp as a blade. "Speak."

Lord Vance stiffens. "The financial stability of the kingdom is hardly 'counter-productive,' necromancer. It is the foundation upon which all else rests."

**You say**

> You say, "Lord Vance you've built the nations finances around slavery and brides, you've come to plead your case that these are essential, but you fail to realize Thorne will be executed for his acts of treason that you're actively defending in front of the crown. You are committing high treason in front of your King and Queen and doing it shamelessly. I'd ask that you leave before I escort you to a cell myself."

# ProjectAIDRPG

Before the story begins, define the person who crossed over.

Name: Zack
Race: Orc
Age: 24
Starting Location: Large city
Appearance: Standard looking

These are starting truths. They are real now, but the story may change them through events, injury, disguise, transformation, aging, death, or other consequences.

---

If there was a dignified way for your old life to end, this was not it.

You remember wet pavement, a horn, headlights, and the deeply unfair thought that this is a stupid way to die.

Then everything goes white.

Not heavenly white. Not peaceful white. More like someone forgot to finish drawing the room.

You are standing anyway.

You have weight. Breath. Hands. A heartbeat doing its best under very confusing circumstances.

You are Zack, a Orc, 24 years old.

Standard looking

Two people are already waiting.

The man is tall, composed, and plainly dressed, with the tired patience of someone who has been right so often that it has become a burden.

You know his name before he says it.

Serathis Vale.

The woman beside him looks warmer, brighter, and considerably more entertained. She has the pleasant expression of someone watching a vase wobble near the edge of a table, curious whether it will fall.

Elyndra Vaelis.

She smiles first.

"Well," she says, looking you over, "that could have gone worse."

Serathis does not look at her. "It still might."

"That's the spirit."

"It is not."

Their exchange is too casual to be a ceremony. Too practiced to be accidental.

Serathis turns his attention to you.

"You were not summoned by a kingdom," he says. "Not chosen by prophecy. Not bought by ritual. Not handed a clean destiny."

Elyndra tilts her head. "Which is not the same as being irrelevant."

"It is," Serathis says, "a warning against assuming importance too early."

She laughs softly. "He means welcome."

"I do not."

"You do a little."

For the first time, Serathis looks genuinely tired.

"The world you are entering was unstable before you arrived," he says. "It will not make special room for you."

Elyndra's smile softens.

"But it will notice you," she says. "Everything does, eventually."

No blessing follows. No shining sword. No promise that this will be fair.

Only a place in a living world.

Serathis steps aside as if opening a door you cannot see.

"That is enough delay."

Elyndra gives you one last look.

"Try to make something of it."

Then the white place vanishes.

Your next breath is heavier.

Large city.

Air fills your lungs with the smell of somewhere real. The ground beneath you holds. Nearby, life is already happening: voices, movement, weather, work, animals, routine.

Your old world is gone.

This one was already in motion before you arrived, and it does not pause to explain itself.

 You are standing on the cobbled edge of a wide street in what is unmistakably a city—a large one, by the noise and scale. The air is thick with the scent of wet stone, woodsmoke, baking bread, and the less pleasant undertone of crowded life. Buildings rise several stories on either side, timber-framed and stone-bottomed, their steep roofs shingled with slate or thatch. Signs creak overhead, painted with symbols for inns, smithies, chandlers, and clothiers.

 You stand on the cobbled edge of a wide street, the weight of your new reality settling into your bones. The city breathes around you—a living, noisy, smelly thing. You are an orc here, a fact made plain by your own reflection in a rain barrel nearby: broad shoulders, greenish skin, prominent tusks, a face that would look brutish to a human. You wear simple, rough-spun trousers and a tunic, no armor, no weapon, no coin. Your pockets are empty.

**You do**

> You jump until you are tired.


You blink, shake your head, and decide to test the limits of this new body.

You start jumping.

At first, it's easy. Your orcish legs are strong, propelling you a good foot or two off the cobbles with each hop. You jump up and down, ignoring the odd looks from passing humans and a dwarf who mutters something about "daft greenskins."

After a dozen jumps, your breathing quickens. After thirty, a dull burn begins in your calves and thighs. Your lungs pull in the thick city air.

 You keep going, jumping higher, pushing until your legs ache and your breath comes in ragged gasps. You're sweating now, your tunic sticking to your back. The wound in your calves—some old injury that came with this body—begins to throb sharply with each impact. It feels like a deep, persistent ache, a reminder that this body isn't pristine.

After maybe fifty jumps, your energy is flagging. Your last jump barely clears the ground.

 You stop, panting, hands on your knees. The calves wound throbs angrily now, a hot, persistent ache that digs deeper with each heartbeat. You're winded, sweat-damp, and standing in the middle of a city street while people flow around you, some giving you a wide berth, others staring openly.

Your energy is low—not dangerously so, but you've burned through a good chunk of it. The wound isn't helping.

A sharp whistle cuts through the street noise. You look up.

**You do**

> You suddenly develop Fireball and shoot a fireball into the sky.


You have no magical training, no affinity for fire, no knowledge of spellcraft, no innate ability to conjure flames. You are an orc—a being of flesh, muscle, and instinct, not a mage. You feel nothing stirring within you, no surge of power, no gathering heat in your palms. You just stand there, panting, sweating, with two aching wounds, and will a fireball into existence.

Nothing happens.

​‍‌‍‌‍‌‍​The doors swing open, revealing the council chamber.

King Edric and Queen Lyra stand at the head of a long, polished table. But they are not alone.

Three other figures are seated around it.

To the Queen's right sits a man in dark, formal robes embroidered with silver thread. He is perhaps fifty, with sharp, intelligent eyes and a neatly trimmed grey beard.



**You say**

> You say, "Pardon my interruption and directness but who might these 3 be?"


Queen Lyra meets your gaze, her expression unreadable. "You have returned swiftly," she says, her voice cool. "And you have brought a guest." Her eyes flick to Finn, taking in his ink-stained hands and worn clothes.

The man in the silver-embroidered robes stands. He is tall, with an air of quiet authority. "I am Lord Alistair Vance," he says, his voice smooth and measured. "Master of Coin for the Royal Treasury." He gives a shallow, precise bow.



**You say**

> You say, "Ah so that's the situation, how far into this discussion are we? Should I take place in this conversation or would you prefer I simply wait a moment for this business to be finished {the king before you left said he'd be replacing this man with Lord Garvin, the old treasurer before this man took over and began taking bribes}"


King Edric's jaw tightens. He shares a quick, loaded glance with Lyra. The Queen's expression is one of sharp, controlled focus.

Lord Vance's eyes narrow almost imperceptibly. He does not sit back down.

"We are discussing the state of the royal coffers," the King says, his voice carefully neutral. "And the... irregularities... discovered in recent transactions."



Lord Vance's gaze shifts from Edric to you. There is a cold calculation in his eyes, the kind of look a banker gives a ledger that doesn't balance.

"Irregularities," he repeats, the word smooth as oiled silk. "A curious term for a matter of state finance. I was just explaining to Their Majesties that the... sudden cessation of tribute payments to Lord Thorne's interests has created a significant... gap in the kingdom's projected outlays."



This man is discussing the slave trade like it was standard business or taxes for the kingdom, and he's ignoring the direct small fortune amassed by seizing Thorne's assets, you're genuinely curious as to how this will play out.

 The Queen's gaze is ice. "A gap, Lord Vance? You speak as if we misplaced a purse. These were bribes. Payments to a slaver."

Lord Vance spreads his hands, a gesture of practiced reason. "Your Majesty, I speak only of the ledgers. The Crown's commitments—treaties, garrisons, supply lines—were balanced against certain... predictable inflows. Removing them without a phased plan risks instability."



He's genuinely proposing that the lack of slavery and bribes is a problem. Very directly, it's almost funny if it wasn't so corrupt and disgusting.

 The Master of Coin's words hang in the air, a testament to the rot you've been ripping out by the roots. He's not defending Thorne, not exactly. He's defending the system that allowed Thorne to exist.

You step further into the room, letting the heavy door swing shut behind Finn, Eira, and Rylan.



**You say**

> You say, "Your majesties may I cut this discussion short? It seems rather counter productive when we have important matters to discuss."


Queen Lyra's eyes cut to you, sharp as a blade. "Speak."

Lord Vance stiffens. "The financial stability of the kingdom is hardly 'counter-productive,' necromancer. It is the foundation upon which all else rests."

**You say**

> You say, "Lord Vance you've built the nations finances around slavery and brides, you've come to plead your case that these are essential, but you fail to realize Thorne will be executed for his acts of treason that you're actively defending in front of the crown. You are committing high treason in front of your King and Queen and doing it shamelessly. I'd ask that you leave before I escort you to a cell myself."

"You accuse me of treason," he says, his voice dropping to a soft, dangerous register. "Based on what? The rantings of a criminal lord? The interpretation of a... foreign sorcerer?" He gestures dismissively toward you. "The ledgers I keep are clean."

Lord Vance's eyes dart from Lyra to Edric, then back to you. For a moment, it looks like he might argue further. Then his shoulders drop a fraction, the fight draining out of him, replaced by a cold, resigned calculation. He gives a stiff, shallow bow.

The doors close behind Lord Vance with a soft, definitive thud. The silence in the council chamber is thick and heavy.

Queen Lyra remains standing, her gaze fixed on the door Vance just exited.

From the walls, from the flagstones, from the very shadows in the corners of the antechamber, figures coalesce. They are not skeletons, not phantoms. They are impressions of armor, of worn surcoats bearing the silver spire of House Valkyrie, of faces set in grim, eternal vigilance.

# Isekai RPG (IS🎭)

## Part 1 of 2

In what world do you win?

You look around the table as you eat dinner. Besides you sits your sister, Amy. In front of you sits your parents scrolling on their phones while eating. It was just like any other day, just like any other family. 

"Where I'm from things were harder, you know?" says Mom. Over the last few years, you've traveled enough to empathize and understand their struggles, but that doesn't matter. Because to them, you would never understand. "Yeah, I know," the indifferent words revisiting your tongue.

The next day, you're at the mall with your family. Everyone moving along—walking, smiling, laughing, running. Their dreams high in the sky, facades close to their face, and delusions deep in their hearts. As you walk, a group of strangers pass by you, laughing, giggling and tossing their shoulders on each other. A void grows in your heart as you stare at what you once had, once lost, and once tried to find. You find yourself thinking, "How could they be so shamelessly themselves, when I have to change?"

As you cross the road, you stay behind your Mom. Your mind in a daze, you fail to notice the oncoming truck. Its presence growing larger as its brakes submit. You see the truck in your peripheral, and in a split second decision, you push your Mom forward to safety—leaving yourself in the truck's path.
She was like any other family. But she was your family. 

"In what world do I win?" 

The last words leave your mouth as the world fades around you.

You open your eyes.

A white light dances across your vision duetting with a yellow light. The glare settles and you find yourself standing on delicate white clouds spanning across until it meets the pink sky. All around you, rich ornaments and clear streams decorate the lands with a yellow hue washing your view. You turn towards the source of the golden aura.

——

"Let's see… Zack. Male. Killed by a truck. Worth a shot."

Somehow, you instantly recognize the beauty in front of you. Mina. The Goddess of Wisdom. Slayer of Death. She Who Sees All, She Who Knows All.  

"Well, I have to say… we both know how this goes. But I'll give you the run down anyways. I'll be reincarnating you into the lands of Essentia. Find a path or find yourself. And maybe help me kill the King of Demons." says Mina.

"Anyways..." she smiles. "As a little gift to cheer you up… you'll have a special ability Quick learner, the ability to learn skills and develop talents faster."

A circle of light rises from your feet. The pink sky brushed yellow and white. Just before the light obscures Mina, she smiles tenderly and gives you a fond wink. "Take care now~", she says. You resolve yourself… 

"This time… I win." 

As the world reveals itself around you, you catch a voice of wisdom fading in your head—you're now in Parada as a 24 year old, Human, Brawler, and you have Quick learner, the ability to learn skills and develop talents faster. Exactly as you would have wished for.



Your senses flood back to you all at once, but it's overwhelming. The air isn't sterile or still; it's thick with scents—damp earth, baked bread, horse dung, and a thousand different perfumes and spices. A cacophony of sound hits you next: the clatter of hooves on stone, raised voices haggling in languages you can't place, the rhythmic clang-clang of a distant blacksmith's hammer, and the lilting melody of a street musician's flute.

You're standing on a wide, cobblestone street, packed with people.

 A burly, green-skinned orc in leather armor barrels past you, muttering about being late to his shift. A pair of elven women with pointed ears and gossamer dresses glide by, their noses turned slightly upward. A stout dwarf, his beard intricately braided, argues loudly with a human merchant over the price of a steel ingot. Above, colorful awnings and lines of laundry stretch between buildings of mismatched architecture; some stone and ivy-covered, others wooden and painted in bright hues.

You're dressed in simple, sturdy linen trousers and a tunic, with worn leather boots on your feet.

**You do**
 You think this is perfect, an isekai world right out of an anime.  You couldn't ask for a better scenario.

 The sensory overload was real, but it wasn't unpleasant. It was alive. The sheer density of existence here—the press of bodies, the riot of smells, the symphony of discordant sounds—felt more real than the sterile mall ever had. A grin spread across your face. This was it. Your second chance.

You instinctively flexed your hands, feeling the strength in them. A Brawler. No magic staffs or longswords for you—just your own body as the weapon. Perfect.

A flash of instinct, a thought turned inward, and a transparent, blue-tinted window materialized in your vision, superimposed over the bustling street.

**You do**
 You ignore the interface for now, it's time to do as isekai hero's do, you're looking for the nearest woods or place to level up.

 The thought is immediate, practical: Level up. Get stronger. You push the interface away from your mind's eye and scan your surroundings.

The street you're on is a main artery, flowing with bodies towards a large, open plaza ahead. To your left, a narrower alley snakes between two tall, stone buildings. It's shadowed, quieter, and smells faintly of refuse and wet stone. More promising than the main thoroughfare if you want to avoid drawing immediate attention. To your right, the street continues past shopfronts and stalls, eventually curving out of sight towards what looks like a set of massive, fortified gates in the distance; the Parada Gates.

 You slip into the alley. The din of the main street muffles behind you, replaced by the drip of water from a rusted gutter and the skittering of something small in the shadows. The cobbles are slick, and the air is cooler. You pass a back door where a human woman is dumping a bucket of soapy water, giving you a suspicious once-over before shutting the door with a bang.

The alley forks. One path leads deeper into a warren of cramped passages between leaning buildings.

 The alley forks. One path leads deeper into a warren of cramped passages between leaning buildings. The other curves around the back of a large, windowless structure; a warehouse, maybe. From around that curve, you hear a new sound. Not the market's din, but a sharp, rhythmic impact. Thwack. Thwack. Thwack.

It's followed by a low, pained grunt.

Your curiosity piqued, you move toward the sound, keeping close to the damp stone wall. Peering around the corner, you see a small, enclosed loading yard behind the warehouse. Crates are stacked haphazardly against one wall.

**You do**
 You boring you want a forest or something.

 The rhythmic thwack, thwack, thwack continues, each impact followed by a guttural, suppressed groan. You edge closer, peering around a stack of wooden crates.

In the center of the loading yard, a man is tied to a thick wooden post. He's a beastfolk, you think; his features are a mix of human and something canine, with pointed ears poking through matted brown hair and a short, furry tail hanging limp behind him. His clothes are simple laborers' garb, now torn and stained. Standing before him is a tall, broad-shouldered human in a fine leather jerkin over a silk shirt.

# 🧙 You are a Summoner 🧙

The morning light filtered through the stained glass of the High Atrium, scattering runes of gold and violet across your desk. Around you, forty students stood within their circles, the air alive with tension and the faint scent of incense and burning chalk. You could hear your own heartbeat, steady and loud, as Master Arven Ral's voice carried through the chamber.

"Remember," he said, cane tapping against the marble floor, "your circle is more than lines and light — it is your truth made visible. A shallow heart summons only shadow. A steady heart summons purpose."

His gaze passed over the class like a blade, sharp and knowing. You knelt, chalk between your fingers, and drew the final sigil of your circle. The pattern had come to you in dreams — simple, balanced, and strange. You weren't even sure why it felt right… only that it did.

Around you, other students were already beginning their summonings. A burst of sapphire light revealed a fox, sleek and silent. Another circle shimmered, and a raven of shadow rose into the air. A lion cub. A serpent of flame. A stag made of smoke. The chamber filled with whispers and wonder.

Master Ral moved among them, nodding once, frowning twice, offering small corrections and praises. "Each familiar," he reminded, "is not chosen by your will — but by what you are."

And now, it was your turn.

You placed your hand over your heart. The circle beneath you hummed softly, its light growing stronger with each breath you took. The air trembled, thick with unseen energy.

"Begin," said Master Ral.

You spoke your incantation. The lines blazed. The circle pulsed — once, twice — and then something stirred within the light.

From within the glow, eyes opened — ancient, aware, and meeting yours for the very first time.

Your familiar had arrived.



For a long moment, the light held the shape of a small, slender fox, its form carved from crystalline ice. Frost patterns swirled across its back, and its tail was a plume of delicate, feathery ice shards. Then, as if remembering it was more than a fixed thing, the form shimmered. The fox-shape blurred, the ice flowing like water, and it became a small, winged serpent of pure frost, coiling in the air before you.

 A collective, hushed murmur ripples through the students nearest to you. The serpent of frost coils once, then dissolves into a cascade of snowflakes that swirl upward before reforming into the fox-shape. It settles on the floor of your circle, its ghostly blue eyes locked on yours. It feels less like looking at an animal and more like gazing into a frozen pond, seeing something ancient and watchful beneath the surface ice.



**You do**

> You well of course you pick it up and pet the pretty baby so happy to see you got such a cutie patootie.


The creature doesn't move as you approach. Its form is solid, yet seems to drink the light, giving it a ghostly, ethereal blue shade. You stretch out a hand. The moment your fingers brush the ice-cold fur between its ears, a shock runs up your arm; not painful, but profound, like a key turning in a lock deep inside your chest. The bond snaps into place.

 The fox-thing tilts its head, a cascade of tiny icicles chiming softly like frozen wind chimes. Its eyes hold your reflection, warped and pale. A thought, clear and sharp as an icicle, pierces your mind without words. It is not a voice, but an impression: Cold. Watchful. Yours.

Master Ral's cane taps on the marble beside your circle. He studies the elemental spirit, his expression unreadable.

 Master Ral crouches, his knees popping faintly. He studies the spirit, his gaze lingering on the frost patterns shifting across its back. "An ice elemental. Rare for a first summoning." His voice is low, meant only for you. "They are creatures of stillness and endurance, not raw power. Remember that." He stands, his tone shifting back to the room at large. "The bond is sealed. Name it. The name is part of the contract."

**You say**

> You say, "This is Penpen my precious little baby. I will love and respect this lil dude forever."


The high-strung girl beside you, whose own summoning produced a nervous-looking glowing sparrow, lets out a choked giggle that she quickly smothers into her sleeve.

Master Ral's mouth tightens almost imperceptibly. "An affectionate name for a spirit of winter," he observes, his tone neutral. "Very well. The record will show: Zack of the common quarters, bonded to Penpen, an ice elemental spirit."

**You say**

> You say, "Woooooooooooo yeahhhh baby, that's what I've been waiting for, that's what it's all about, woooooooooooooo"

Master Ral stares at you, his expression flat. The silence that follows your whooping cheer is absolute, broken only by the soft chiming of Penpen's icy fur as he shifts his weight. The sparrow girl's eyes are wide with horrified fascination.

"Enthusiasm noted," Master Ral says dryly, his knuckles whitening slightly on the head of his cane. He turns his attention back to the chamber. "The summoning is complete."

**You do**

> You hold your lil ice dude give him some pets and affection for being so cute and so nice.


You cradle Penpen in your arms. The cold seeps through your academy robes, a sharp, clean chill that settles into your bones. He doesn't purr, but a soft, crystalline hum vibrates against your chest, and the frost patterns on his back swirl slowly, lazily. His ghostly blue eyes are half-lidded, watching the other students and their familiars with detached, ancient curiosity.

A shadow falls over you.

 A tall, broad-shouldered boy with close-cropped red hair and a face full of freckles stands at the edge of your circle, his own familiar—a stout badger with earth-stone plates along its spine—snuffling at his boots. He looks from Penpen to you, a smirk playing on his lips. "A snow fox? For real? My little sister has a plushie that looks scarier."

**You say**

> You say, "Right? Isn't he just so damn cute I just wanna squeeze the lil dude"


The red-haired boy blinks, the smirk faltering for a second. His badger lets out a low, grumbling huff. "Cute?" he repeats, as if the word tastes strange. "It's a familiar. They're for dueling. For defending the realms. Not... cuddling."

From behind him, a slender girl with ink-stained fingers and a floating, wisp-like familiar shaped from shimmering mist speaks up, her voice quiet but sharp.

 The red-haired boy turns, annoyance flashing across his freckled face. "What, Elara?"

"You were showing off your badger to anyone who would listen five minutes ago, Corin," she says, not looking up from the notebook she's scribbling in. Her mist-wisp darts around her head like an agitated thought. "Let him enjoy his bond. Master Ral said the name is part of the contract."

**You say**

> You say, "Oh shoot you got a badger? What kind? Is it cool?"


Corin puffs his chest out a little, the smirk returning. "Rock-backed badger. Terra-class. His name's Grond." The badger—Grond—stomps a heavy paw, a tiny tremor vibrating through the marble floor underfoot. "He can dig through solid stone in ten seconds. What's your little snowball gonna do? Give someone a chill?"

Elara sighs audibly, the sound like rustling parchment.

**You say**

> You say, "That's pretty sick. My buddy here is an elemental spirit though I'm not sure what he's able to do but I do know he's adorable and cooler than cool"


Corin snorts. "Adorable. Right." He shakes his head, a condescending grin spreading across his face. "You'll see, commoner. The first familiar duels start next week. Cuteness doesn't win points." He turns on his heel, Grond lumbering after him with a final, dismissive snort.

Elara watches him go, then her gaze flicks back to you and Penpen.

**You say**

> You say, "What's your summon? Looks like a wisp or something"


Elara's wispy familiar swirls closer, its form shimmering between smoke and faint light. She doesn't smile, but her expression softens slightly. "A memory-wisp. It doesn't fight. It... records. Observes. Its name is Echo." She glances at Penpen, still cradled in your arms. "Ice elementals are patient. They outlast. That's a kind of power too."

**You say**

> You say, ""A spirit of frost" the teacher called it
It sounds super badass honestly but as it stands this is just my cute little buddy, ain't that right Penpen? You're a little cute badass aren't you buddy?"


The ice elemental in your arms tilts its head. The crystalline chime of his fur seems to vibrate with a faint, amused resonance. The cold against your chest is a constant, grounding presence.

Elara's lips twitch, the barest hint of a smile. "A contradictory nature suits an elemental," she says, closing her notebook. "They are not like us. Simple labels don't fit."

**You say**

> You say, "All I know he is turned into some winged serpent for a second when he first got summoned? I don't think any specific description fits this little dude he's clearly up to something {you hold him tighter with pride and love, happier than you expected to be deciding Penpen fits you perfectly as a partner}"


Elara's wisp, Echo, drifts closer to Penpen, its form shimmering with what might be curiosity. "A form-shifter, even in minor ways," she observes, her voice thoughtful. "That suggests a fluid nature. Not bound to a single shape. That's... uncommon for a first-bond elemental."

 Master Ral's voice cuts through the murmuring chamber, crisp and clear. "The bonding is complete. You will now proceed to your assigned dormitory quarters. Your familiar will reside with you. Tomorrow, your practical instruction begins. Dismissed."

The spell of the summoning breaks. The room erupts into a wave of chatter, laughter, anxious whispers, and the strange, soft sounds of forty new familiars. You stand, Penpen a solid, cold weight in your arms.

**You say**

> You say, "You're a little chilly you know that buddy? Let's get you back and show you your new home then, for right now it's just a dorm but I bet we'll climb to something better soon."


Penpen shifts in your arms, the crystalline chime of his fur a soft, constant sound against the growing din of the chamber. His ghostly blue eyes seem to take in the dispersing crowd of students and their familiars; the sapphire fox weaving between legs, the shadow-raven perched on a shoulder, Corin already striding toward the exit with Grond waddling purposefully at his heels.

 The path from the High Atrium to the commoner dormitories is a long, winding descent through Saint-Eworth's lower levels. The grandeur of stained glass and polished marble gives way to sturdy stone, functional sconces, and the distant, ever-present hum of the academy's foundational magics. You walk with a loose cluster of other common-born students, a few of whom keep glancing at Penpen with a mix of curiosity and apprehension.



​‍​You push open the heavy oak door to the commoner dormitory wing. The corridor is narrow, lit by flickering magelight sconces, and smells of old stone, wood polish, and the faint, ever-present scent of ozone from active enchantments. Doors line the hall, each bearing a brass plate with a student's name.

​‍‌​The heavy oak door groans shut behind you, muffling the chaotic noise of the hallway. Your room is sparse: a narrow bed, a wooden desk and chair, a small wardrobe, and a single window looking out onto a walled courtyard far below. A simple stone hearth, cold and empty, sits in one corner.

 The chill radiating from Penpen is the only thing that feels truly solid in the unfamiliar space. You set him down on the worn wool blanket of your bed.  A small, sharp breath escapes you. You reach for the connection between you, the thread of intent that binds your will to his. You push that awareness toward the hearth; not a command, but a suggestion. A quiet offering of the cold, quiet space.

# Personal Isekai

## Part 1 of 2

In what world do you win?

You look around the table as you eat dinner. Besides you sits your sister, Amy. In front of you sits your parents scrolling on their phones while eating. It was just like any other day, just like any other family. 

"Where I'm from things were harder, you know?" says Mom. Over the last few years, you've traveled enough to empathize and understand their struggles, but that doesn't matter. Because to them, you would never understand. "Yeah, I know," the indifferent words revisiting your tongue.

The next day, you're at the mall with your family. Everyone moving along—walking, smiling, laughing, running. Their dreams high in the sky, facades close to their face, and delusions deep in their hearts. As you walk, a group of strangers pass by you, laughing, giggling and tossing their shoulders on each other. A void grows in your heart as you stare at what you once had, once lost, and once tried to find. You find yourself thinking, "How could they be so shamelessly themselves, when I have to change?"

As you cross the road, you stay behind your Mom. Your mind in a daze, you fail to notice the oncoming truck. Its presence growing larger as its brakes submit. You see the truck in your peripheral, and in a split second decision, you push your Mom forward to safety—leaving yourself in the truck's path.
She was like any other family. But she was your family. 

"In what world do I win?" 

The last words leave your mouth as the world fades around you.

You open your eyes.

A white light dances across your vision duetting with a yellow light. The glare settles and you find yourself standing on delicate white clouds spanning across until it meets the pink sky. All around you, rich ornaments and clear streams decorate the lands with a yellow hue washing your view. You turn towards the source of the golden aura.

——

"Let's see… . . Killed by a truck. Worth a shot."

Somehow, you instantly recognize the beauty in front of you. Mina. The Goddess of Wisdom. Slayer of Death. She Who Sees All, She Who Knows All.  

"Well, I have to say… we both know how this goes. But I'll give you the run down anyways. I'll be reincarnating you into the lands of Essentia. Find a path or find yourself. And maybe help me kill the King of Demons." says Mina.

"Anyways..." she smiles. "As a little gift to cheer you up… you'll have an special ability."

A circle of light rises from your feet. The pink sky brushed yellow and white. Just before the light obscures Mina, she smiles tenderly and gives you a fond wink. "Take care now~", she says. You resolve yourself… 

"This time… I win." 

As the world reveals itself around you, you catch a voice of wisdom fading in your head—you're now in Parada as a 23 year old, Human, Monk class, and the special ability the goddess gave you. Exactly as you left your world and would have wished for.



The light fades not into darkness, but into color, scent, and sound. The air is cool and carries the damp, earthy smell of stone and moss, mixed with the distant aroma of baked bread and spices. You are standing on a cobblestone street, worn smooth by countless footsteps. Ivy climbs the walls of the buildings flanking you; structures of timber and pale plaster, with steeply sloped roofs of dark slate.

**You do**
 You look around in disbelief.  You didn't notice much.

The air was a tapestry of scents; woodsmoke, damp earth, roasting meat, the faint tang of something metallic. Voices chattered in a dozen different tongues.



Alright. Let's see... Killed by a truck. Worth a shot.

But the arm was dead. Its mana network was a fused, charcoal sketch inside the grain.

**You do**

> That's the whole idea, inject a new network in, replacing the old broken path. Cast Arcane Injection.


The instruction was clear in your mind. You had the blueprint, the internal map of a functioning arm. You had the dark energy, a tool precise enough to etch a new circulatory system into dead wood. The broken network was just... dead weight now. You had to replace it.

You cast Arcane Injection. The soft, internal hum of the skill activating vibrated in your chest. Your vision didn't change, but your perception did.

 You knelt on the damp moss, the cold seeping deeper into your bones. The wooden arm was a dead thing now. The scar was there, the fused ruin of your own making, but it was just an obstacle. You had to carve through it.

You placed your hands back on the cool bark. Your focus narrowed to a single, sharp point.

 The hum of Arcane Injection was different this time. Softer, more internal—a quiet resonance in your bones instead of a vibration in the air. You didn't see the world shift into grids and schematics. You felt it.

Your consciousness flowed down your arms, into your palms, and into the wood. You weren't just touching bark; you were inside it. You felt the grain like ridges in a canyon, the hardened sap like veins of cold glass.

 The forest around you vanished. Your awareness became the wood—its density, its grain, the brittle, fused mess that was the old mana network, a dead scar running through its core like a fossilized lightning strike.

You didn't have to think about the blueprint. You knew it. It was the image of a perfect, flowing system of channels, from major arteries down to the finest capillaries. Your will—the cold, dark energy of your Wrath—became your chisel.

 You cast Arcane Injection, and the world dissolved into sensation.

It wasn't a grid, not this time. It was pressure and texture, resistance and flow. Your consciousness poured into the wooden arm, not as an observer, but as a sculptor working in total darkness. You felt the grain; tight, concentric rings of ancient growth. You felt the hardened sap, cold and glassy in pockets.

**You do**
 You fix the mana paths and repair the tree.  You grasp at the edge of your Mana Surgery, trying to unleash it swiftly.

 The cold, dark energy of your Wrath wasn't a surge this time. It was a slow, deliberate flood, seeping from your palms into the dead wood. Your awareness was the wood. You felt the grain, the hard lines of growth, the brittle, glassy patches of hardened sap. And you felt the scar—the old, fused mana network. It wasn't an obstacle to be removed; it was material to be reshaped.

The blueprint was your guide, but your hands—your will—were the tools. You didn't carve new channels. You pressed. The dark energy, cold and fluid as ink, seeped into the wood and found the scar. It flowed into the fused, charcoal-like lattice of the ruined network.

A subtle, grinding sensation vibrated back through your connection. You were not cutting; you were unraveling.

 You pull your hands back. The tendrils of dark energy withdraw into your skin, leaving the bark unmarked.

For a long moment, nothing happens. The wooden arm is just a limb-shaped protrusion from the oak, silent and still. The forest holds its breath.

Then, a faint, golden glow kindles deep within the wood. It starts at the shoulder joint, a soft ember-light that pulses once, twice.

 The grinding sensation intensified, a deep, resonant vibration that traveled up your arms and settled in your jaw. It wasn't painful, but it was profoundly unsettling—like feeling the bones of the earth shift. Through the dark energy connection, you felt the old, fused network begin to yield. It didn't shatter; it softened, becoming malleable under the relentless, cold pressure of your will.

You weren't rebuilding from scratch. You were repurposing.

 The glow strengthened, spreading down the length of the arm like liquid sunlight flowing through a new vein. It traced the paths you had envisioned, the channels you had willed into being. The light wasn't uniform; it pulsed with a gentle rhythm, brighter at the major nodes—shoulder, elbow, wrist—and dimming to a soft shimmer along the finer capillaries that branched towards the wooden fingers.

The light solidified.

 The grinding sensation faded. The last echoes of your will ceased their vibration through the wood. You pulled your hands back. Your palms felt cold, the last traces of the dark energy seeping back into your skin, leaving the bark smooth and unmarked. You knelt there, breathing slowly, the scent of ozone finally gone, replaced by the rich, clean smell of wet earth and... something else. Something warm, like sun-warmed sap.

The wooden arm was no longer just a carving.

 You opened your eyes. The arm was still wood, but it was alive. A soft, internal golden light pulsed within it, tracing the pathways you'd carved with your will. It wasn't a fierce, magical glow; more like the gentle luminescence of heartwood in deep summer, visible only because the sun had dipped below the trees, casting the clearing into twilight.

You flexed your own fingers, feeling a dull ache in your palms from the sustained concentration.

**You do**
 You perfect it, ensure the arm is as it was when it was made, fix it.

 The grinding sensation ceased completely. The connection—the deep, unsettling feeling of being inside the wood—snapped away. You were back in your own body, kneeling on the moss, the chill of the evening air sharp against your skin. The soft, golden glow within the wooden arm pulsed once, steadily, and then settled into a constant, low hum of warmth.

 That's exactly what you'll need to do to Corwin, you look up at the sky to check the time

 The sun had dipped low, casting long, deepening shadows across the clearing. The golden light within the wooden arm had stabilized into a soft, ambient glow, illuminating the grain of the oak in warm relief. It was whole. It was proof.

You got to your feet, knees aching from the damp ground. The air was cool now, the day's heat fading fast. You had a skill. A real, tangible, potentially world-changing skill. Mana Surgery.

 You head to Durin to let him know the "impossible skill" had been made.  Ask him to send for Silas the lords middleman as he offered to.

You didn't waste any time. The proof was hanging from the oak tree, pulsing with a soft, golden light in the gathering twilight. You turned your back on the clearing and started down the familiar path toward the docks, your steps quickening from a walk to a jog. The ache in your knees and the chill in your hands were secondary now, drowned out by the steady, quiet thrum of certainty in your chest.



​‍‍‍‍‍‍‍​The docks were quiet when you arrived, the day's cargo long since stowed, the last of the workers filtering out into the dusk toward Parada's evening markets and taverns.



You push open the heavy door of Durin's workshop. It was part shed, part office, a long, low building tucked between two warehouses, its walls stacked with spare lumber, barrels of pitch, and coils of thick rope. A single oil lamp hung from a low beam, casting a warm, swaying circle of light over a cluttered desk where Durin sat, squinting at a ledger.

 Durin didn't look up immediately. His thick finger traced a column of figures, his lips moving silently. The scratch of a quill was the only sound besides the soft crackle of the lamp's wick. The air smelled of sawdust, wet hemp, and the sharp tang of varnish.

You stood just inside the door, the damp chill of the forest still clinging to your clothes. Your breathing was steady, but your heart hammered against your ribs. You waited.

 The door creaked shut behind you, cutting off the distant sound of lapping water.

Durin's finger stopped. He looked up slowly, his eyes narrowing against the lamplight. He took in your appearance; the damp trousers, the moss-stained knees, the way you stood there not with exhaustion, but with a coiled, quiet intensity.

"Zack," he said, his voice a low rumble. He set the quill down.



​‍‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​You didn't speak. You didn't need to. You stood there, letting the silence stretch, the weight of what you'd done hanging between you and the lamplight.

Durin leaned back in his chair. The wood groaned under his weight. His gaze didn't leave you.

**You say**

> You say, "It's finished. The skill, I perfected a surgical skill that can fix Corwin."


Durin didn't move for a long moment. The lamplight flickered across the deep lines of his face. He looked at you not with disbelief, but with a slow, heavy calculation. He saw the quiet certainty in your eyes, the stillness in your stance. You weren't boasting. You were reporting a fact.

"The proof," he said finally, the word hanging in the sawdust-scented air. It wasn't a question.

**You say**

> You say, "What proof? You need me to fuse lightning into my own arm and fix it for you? Because I wouldn't doubt that's what Silas will expect before letting me treat Corwin's injury"


You watched him process that. The quill lay forgotten on the ledger. He leaned forward, elbows on the desk, his massive hands clasped before him. The lamplight cast his shadow large against the wall of coiled rope.

"No," he rumbled. His voice was low, certain. "Silas won't need a demonstration. Not from you. He knows me."

**You say**

> You say, "Okay then, you're asking me to preform it for just you then?"


Durin's gaze didn't waver. "I'm not asking you to perform anything. I'm telling you to be ready. If you've done what you say you've done, then you've crafted a key to a locked door. My job was to find the man who could forge the key. Silas' job is to see if it fits the lock."

He pushed himself up from the desk, the chair groaning in relief.

 He looked at you for a long moment, then walked to a small, iron-banded chest sitting against the far wall. He pulled a key from a chain around his neck, unlocked it, and lifted out a heavy, folded piece of parchment sealed with a blob of dark red wax stamped with a simple, geometric crest; a stylized anchor within a circle.

"I'm sending for him tonight," Durin said, turning back to you, the parchment in his hand.

**You say**

> You say, "When would he arrive?"


Durin looked at the folded parchment in his hand, then back at you. "A runner leaves within the hour. If Silas is at his post, he'll receive the message by dawn. He'll arrive when he arrives." He walked to the door of the workshop, pulled it open a crack, and whistled sharply; a short, piercing sound that cut through the quiet evening.

**You say**

> You say, "I assume it would probably be quick for something this important though? They wouldn't just let the boy sit there being destroyed by his own mana from the inside out would they?"


​‍‌‌‌‌‌‌‍​You watched him in the doorway, a silhouette against the deepening blue of the evening sky. The urgency you felt wasn't mirrored in his calm, deliberate movements. A moment later, a wiry boy in roughspun clothes appeared from the shadows between the warehouses, jogging up to the door.

 You stood there, feeling the damp chill of your clothes against your skin, the quiet hum of your own certainty clashing with Durin's pragmatic calm. The runner—a boy with sharp eyes and a lean frame—stopped just outside the lamplight's reach, waiting.

Durin held out the sealed parchment. "For Silas. Lord Vance's man, at the usual place. Fast as your feet will carry you. No stops."



​‍‌‌‌‌‌‍‌​The boy took the parchment without a word, his fingers quick and sure. He tucked it into the inner lining of his tunic, gave Durin a sharp nod, and then he was gone, melting back into the shadows between the stacks of lumber and tarpaulin-covered crates.



Durin closed the workshop door against the evening chill. He turned back to you, his face unreadable in the flickering lamplight.

"He'll be here by tomorrow noon, if he's still in the city. If he's gone to the country estate, it could be another day." He walked back to his desk, but didn't sit. He just stood there, looking at you.

AI Dungeon Scripting Reference
How scripts work, official limits, and service restrictions
Based on official AI Dungeon Help and Terms sources, checked April 26, 2026.
1. What AI Dungeon scripts are
AI Dungeon scripts are scenario-attached JavaScript modifiers that let a creator change input text, model context, output text, persistent state, and story cards. They are not arbitrary app plugins; they run inside AI Dungeon’s scripting API and lifecycle hooks.
2. Where scripts can be used
Scripts are attached to scenarios.
Adventures started from a scenario have separate game states but share the same script code.
Only Simple Start and Character Creator scenarios can have scripts directly.
Multiple Choice scenarios cannot have scripts directly, but their options can have scripts, and those scripts are independent.
Only the creator of a scenario can see that scenario’s scripts.
3. Script layout in the editor
There are four script areas: Library, Input, Context, and Output.
Library is shared code and values used by the other three tabs.
Input runs during the onInput hook.
Context runs during the onModelContext hook.
Output runs during the onOutput hook.
For every non-Library script tab, the last line must always be modifier(text).
4. The three lifecycle hooks
onInput: runs before the player’s input is used to build context.
onModelContext: runs after context is assembled but before the model is called.
onOutput: runs after the model returns text but before the player sees it.
Each hook runs in its own isolated sandbox.
5. Hard runtime limits
Per-hook memory limit: 16 MB.
Per-hook execution timeout: 2 seconds.
If you exceed these, the hook can fail.
Practical implication: keep processing short, avoid giant scans, and avoid building very large strings in tight loops.
6. Data available to scripts
Scripts can reference API values directly by name without destructuring them from an object.
text: the current input, model context, or output string, depending on the hook.
history: recent adventure actions.
storyCards: the current adventure’s story cards.
state: persistent per-adventure script state.
info: utility metadata such as actionCount, characterNames, and context-only values like maxChars and memoryLength.
7. Important built-in state fields
state.memory.context: prepended memory.
state.memory.authorsNote: inserted near the end of context.
state.memory.frontMemory: appended at the very end of context.
state.message: user-facing message string; official doc notes this is not yet implemented on Phoenix.
state.placeholders: scenario-start placeholder questions and answers.
Important limitation: if you update state.memory in onOutput, the change does not affect the current turn; it takes effect on the next player action.
Important limitation: using state.memory.context or state.memory.authorsNote overrides the UI values, but does not update the UI fields themselves. Also, if those values are unset or empty, the UI values are still used, so state cannot completely clear memory or author’s note.
8. Built-in functions
log / console.log: write to the console log.
addStoryCard(keys, entry, type): adds a story card and returns its index; returns false if a card with the same keys already exists.
removeStoryCard(index): removes a story card; throws if the card does not exist.
updateStoryCard(index, keys, entry, type): updates a story card; throws if the card does not exist.
Backward-compatible names still exist for older scripts, but they are deprecated: worldInfo, addWorldEntry, removeWorldEntry, updateWorldEntry, sandboxConsole.log, and rawText on history actions.
9. Return behavior
Scripts return an object, commonly { text } or { text, stop }.
Returning text in onInput replaces player input.
Returning text in onModelContext replaces the text sent to the AI.
Returning text in onOutput replaces the text shown to the player.
Returning an empty string in onInput throws an error to the player.
Returning an empty string in onModelContext makes context behave as though the script did not run.
Returning an empty string in onOutput throws a custom-script failure error to the player.
Returning stop: true stops the game loop.
Using stop in onInput or onModelContext produces an error message to the player.
Using stop in onOutput changes the output to the literal word stop; the official docs explicitly say not to do this.
10. Editor and testing tools
The Script Test panel lets you run the selected non-Library script plus the library against test input.
The test output includes text, stop, logs, state, and storyCards.
Console logs are visible in the editor for recent adventures started by the scenario owner.
Console logs and inspect data are retained for 15 minutes.
The Inspect modal shows recent model context and game state for the owner’s adventures only.
11. Practical guidelines that follow from the official limits
Keep onModelContext concise; AI Dungeon provides maxChars and will truncate overlong context anyway.
Do not rely on onOutput memory edits affecting the same turn.
Do not return stop from onOutput.
Do not return empty text from onInput or onOutput.
When using story cards, handle duplicates and missing cards explicitly because add/update/remove have defined failure behavior.
Use state for persistent structured data; use story cards when you need model-visible structured content.
Treat Input, Context, and Output tabs as modifier wrappers around shared Library code, not as isolated mini-projects.
12. Official service restrictions that matter for script authors
AI Dungeon’s Terms allow community scripts and related contributions, but they also impose service-level limits that matter if you publish or distribute script-based content.
Community contributions such as scripts, mods, extensions, worlds, and UI tweaks are allowed if they comply with the Terms, Community Guidelines, and any technical requirements or policies AI Dungeon publishes.
Community contributions may not distribute AI Dungeon’s proprietary AI models or internal prompts.
Community contributions may not be sold as stand-alone products unless AI Dungeon expressly allows it.
Community contributions may not be used to move players to a competing platform.
AI Dungeon may limit or disable community contributions or technical methods that harm the service, users, or the company.
The Terms also prohibit reverse engineering, scraping, automation aimed at reconstructing internal systems, and unauthorized bots/modification software directed at the service itself.
Practical implication: writing a script for your scenario is allowed, but building tools or workflows that try to extract internal prompts, scrape the service, automate against the platform in unauthorized ways, or package proprietary internals is not.
13. What is allowed versus what is restricted
Allowed: scripts attached to scenarios, stateful gameplay logic, story card automation, UI tweaks or community contributions that work with the service and follow the rules.
Restricted: reverse engineering the service, scraping or mining service data, using automation to reconstruct internal code or prompts, unauthorized bots/hacks/mods aimed at modifying the service, distributing proprietary internal models or prompts, or selling community contributions as stand-alone products without permission.
Moderation note: published scenario scripts may be reviewed for compliance with Community Guidelines.
14. Best-practice checklist for writing compatible scripts
Put reusable helpers in Library.
Keep the final line modifier(text) in Input, Context, and Output.
Keep every hook under the 2-second and 16 MB limits.
Use state for persistence across turns.
Use storyCards when the model needs to see structured information.
Guard against duplicate story card creation.
Do not assume empty text or stop behave the same in all hooks.
Use info.maxChars and info.memoryLength to manage context size.
Test with Script Test first, then with a live scenario run, then inspect logs.
15. Short version
AI Dungeon scripting is JavaScript running inside three controlled lifecycle hooks. It can modify player input, model context, output text, state, and story cards, but each hook is sandboxed and strictly limited to 16 MB and 2 seconds. Scripts live on scenarios, not arbitrary adventures, and non-Library tabs must end with modifier(text). The biggest practical pitfalls are returning invalid text/stop values for the wrong hook, assuming onOutput memory changes apply immediately, and writing code that exceeds time or memory limits.
Official sources used
AI Dungeon Help: Scripting
AI Dungeon Help: What are Scripts and how do you Install them?
AI Dungeon Terms of Service, last revised April 22, 2026

function deepClone(value) {
  return JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value ?? null));
}

function getPath(root, path) {
  if (!path) return root;
  const parts = String(path).split('.').filter(Boolean);
  let ref = root;
  for (const part of parts) {
    if (ref == null || typeof ref !== 'object' || !(part in ref)) return undefined;
    ref = ref[part];
  }
  return ref;
}

function stableString(value) {
  try { return JSON.stringify(value, Object.keys(value || {}).sort()); }
  catch { return String(value); }
}

function shallowEqualPrimitive(a, b) {
  return a === b || (Number.isNaN(a) && Number.isNaN(b));
}

function tooLarge(value, limit = 120000) {
  try { return JSON.stringify(value).length > limit; }
  catch { return true; }
}

function brief(value) {
  if (value == null) return value;
  if (typeof value !== 'object') return value;
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return { type: 'array', length: value.length, sample: value.slice(0, 5) };
  const keys = Object.keys(value);
  return { type: 'object', keyCount: keys.length, keys: keys.slice(0, 20) };
}

function diffValues(before, after, prefix = '', out = [], max = 200, depth = 0) {
  if (out.length >= max) return out;
  if (shallowEqualPrimitive(before, after)) return out;

  const beforeObj = before && typeof before === 'object';
  const afterObj = after && typeof after === 'object';

  if (depth > 12 || !beforeObj || !afterObj || Array.isArray(before) || Array.isArray(after)) {
    // Avoid expensive full serialization on huge arrays/objects; keep reports useful and bounded.
    if (beforeObj || afterObj) out.push({ path: prefix || '(root)', before: brief(before), after: brief(after) });
    else out.push({ path: prefix || '(root)', before, after });
    return out;
  }

  if (tooLarge(before) || tooLarge(after)) {
    const beforeKeys = before && typeof before === 'object' ? Object.keys(before) : [];
    const afterKeys = after && typeof after === 'object' ? Object.keys(after) : [];
    const keys = new Set([...beforeKeys, ...afterKeys]);
    for (const key of keys) {
      if (out.length >= max) break;
      const b = before ? before[key] : undefined;
      const a = after ? after[key] : undefined;
      if (b !== a) diffValues(b, a, prefix ? `${prefix}.${key}` : key, out, max, depth + 1);
    }
    return out;
  }

  try {
    if (JSON.stringify(before) === JSON.stringify(after)) return out;
  } catch (_) {}

  const keys = new Set([...Object.keys(before || {}), ...Object.keys(after || {})]);
  for (const key of keys) {
    if (out.length >= max) break;
    diffValues(before ? before[key] : undefined, after ? after[key] : undefined, prefix ? `${prefix}.${key}` : key, out, max, depth + 1);
  }
  return out;
}

module.exports = { deepClone, getPath, diffValues, stableString };

const fs = require('fs');

const SYSTEM_MARKERS = {
  CoreState: 'CoreState:',
  TurnEngine: 'TurnEngine:',
  Utils: 'Utils:',
  AdminDebugSystem: 'AdminDebugSystem:',
  PlayerSystem: 'PlayerSystem:',
  BuildIdentitySystem: 'BuildIdentitySystem:',
  IntentParser: 'IntentParser:',
  ProgressionSystem: 'ProgressionSystem:',
  InventorySystem: 'InventorySystem:',
  SceneStateSystem: 'SceneStateSystem:',
  WorldEntitySystem: 'WorldEntitySystem:',
  TimeTravelSystem: 'TimeTravelSystem:',
  AbilitySystem: 'AbilitySystem:',
  PersistentTraitSystem: 'PersistentTraitSystem:',
  ConsequenceParser: 'ConsequenceParser:',
  ValidationSystem: 'ValidationSystem:',
  SpecializationSystem: 'SpecializationSystem:',
  ActorProfileSystem: 'ActorProfileSystem:',
  ContextPacketSystem: 'ContextPacketSystem:',
  ReputationSystem: 'ReputationSystem:',
  QuestLogSystem: 'QuestLogSystem:',
  CardSyncSystem: 'CardSyncSystem:',
  NPCGenerationSystem: 'NPCGenerationSystem:',
  CombatResolutionSystem: 'CombatResolutionSystem:'
};

function buildSourceIndex(scriptPath) {
  const source = fs.readFileSync(scriptPath, 'utf8');
  const lines = source.split(/\r?\n/);
  const index = {};
  for (const [system, marker] of Object.entries(SYSTEM_MARKERS)) {
    const lineNo = lines.findIndex(line => line.includes(marker));
    if (lineNo !== -1) index[system] = { line: lineNo + 1, marker };
  }
  return { lines, index };
}

function getPatchZone(scriptPath, system) {
  const { lines, index } = buildSourceIndex(scriptPath);
  const found = index[system];
  if (!found) return { system, line: null, snippet: '', note: 'No section marker found.' };
  const start = Math.max(0, found.line - 4);
  const end = Math.min(lines.length, found.line + 35);
  const snippet = lines.slice(start, end).map((line, i) => `${start + i + 1}: ${line}`).join('\n');
  return { system, line: found.line, snippet, note: `Likely section starts near line ${found.line}.` };
}

module.exports = { buildSourceIndex, getPatchZone };

const fs = require('fs');

const { getPatchZone } = require('./source-locator');

const SYSTEM_HINTS = [
  ['items', 'InventorySystem'], ['inventory', 'InventorySystem'], ['equipment', 'InventorySystem'], ['currency', 'InventorySystem'],
  ['abilities', 'AbilitySystem'], ['persistentTraits', 'PersistentTraitSystem'], ['conditions', 'PersistentTraitSystem'],
  ['actors', 'ActorProfileSystem'], ['actor', 'ActorProfileSystem'],
  ['world.currentScene', 'SceneStateSystem'], ['currentScene', 'SceneStateSystem'],
  ['world.locations', 'WorldEntitySystem'], ['locationsById', 'WorldEntitySystem'], ['entitiesById', 'WorldEntitySystem'], ['routes', 'WorldEntitySystem'],

function likelySystemFromPath(pathText = '') {
  const p = String(pathText || '');
  for (const [needle, system] of SYSTEM_HINTS) {
    if (p.includes(needle)) return system;
  }
  return 'Unknown / Cross-System';
}

function likelySystemFromResult(result) {
  if (result.expectedSystem) return result.expectedSystem;
  const failed = (result.assertions || []).filter(a => !a.passed);
  const first = failed[0];
  if (first && first.path) return likelySystemFromPath(first.path);
  const s = String(result.suite || '').toLowerCase();
  if (s.includes('inventory')) return 'InventorySystem';
  if (s.includes('intent')) return 'IntentParser';
  if (s.includes('time')) return 'TimeTravelSystem';
  if (s.includes('context')) return 'ContextPacketSystem';
  if (s.includes('actor')) return 'ActorProfileSystem';
  if (s.includes('ability')) return 'AbilitySystem';
  if (s.includes('scene')) return 'SceneStateSystem';
  if (s.includes('world')) return 'WorldEntitySystem';
  if (s.includes('validation')) return 'ValidationSystem';
  return 'Unknown / Cross-System';
}

function summarizeFailure(test) {
  const failed = (test.assertions || []).filter(a => !a.passed);
  const system = likelySystemFromResult(test);
  let severity = 'Low';
  if (test.errors && test.errors.length) severity = 'High';
  else if (failed.some(a => ['noRuntimeErrors','validHookReturn','exists','objectHasKeys'].includes(a.type))) severity = 'High';
  else if (failed.length) severity = test.severity || 'Medium';
  const confidence = (test.errors && test.errors.length) || failed.length ? 'Medium' : 'Low';
  return { system, severity, confidence };
}

function assertionLine(a) {
  let line = `- Assertion failed: ${a.type}`;
  if (a.path) line += ` on \`${a.path}\``;
  if ('expected' in a) line += ` | expected: ${JSON.stringify(a.expected)}`;
  if ('min' in a || 'max' in a) line += ` | range: ${a.min}..${a.max}`;
  line += ` | actual: ${String(JSON.stringify(a.actual) ?? 'undefined').slice(0, 1400)}`;
  if (a.error) line += ` | error: ${a.error}`;
  return line;
}

function writeReports(results, options = {}) {
  const reportDir = options.reportDir || path.join(process.cwd(), 'reports');
  const scriptPath = options.scriptPath || path.join(process.cwd(), 'aidrpg-script.js');
  fs.mkdirSync(reportDir, { recursive: true });

  const passed = results.filter(r => r.passed).length;
  const failed = results.length - passed;
  const failures = results.filter(r => !r.passed);
  const suspicious = results.filter(r => r.suspicious && r.passed).length;


  const maturityGroups = {};
  for (const f of failures) {
    const m = f.maturity || 'UNLABELED';
    if (!maturityGroups[m]) maturityGroups[m] = [];
    maturityGroups[m].push(f);
  }

  const grouped = {};
  for (const f of failures) {
    const summary = summarizeFailure(f);
    if (!grouped[summary.system]) grouped[summary.system] = [];
    grouped[summary.system].push(f);
  }

  const lines = [];
  lines.push('# AIDRPG Whole-System Tester Report');
  lines.push('');
  lines.push(`Generated: ${new Date().toISOString()}`);
  lines.push(`Suite: ${options.suite || 'unknown'}`);
  lines.push(`Cases tested: ${results.length}`);
  lines.push(`Passed: ${passed}`);
  lines.push(`Failed: ${failed}`);
  lines.push(`Suspicious: ${suspicious}`);
  lines.push('');

  if (failures.length === 0) {
    lines.push('## Result');
    lines.push('');
    lines.push('No failing assertions were found in this run. This does not prove the whole game is perfect; it means this suite did not catch a failure. Larger limits and more generated suites can still reveal problems.');
    lines.push('');
  } else {

    lines.push('## Roadmap Maturity Breakdown');
    lines.push('');
    for (const [maturity, list] of Object.entries(maturityGroups).sort((a,b)=>b[1].length-a[1].length)) {
      lines.push(`- ${maturity}: ${list.length} failing test(s)`);
    }
    lines.push('');
    lines.push('## Recommended Fix Order');
    lines.push('');
    Object.entries(grouped).sort((a,b)=>b[1].length-a[1].length).forEach(([system, list], idx) => {
      const high = list.filter(x => summarizeFailure(x).severity === 'High').length;
      lines.push(`${idx + 1}. ${system}: ${list.length} failing test(s)${high ? `, ${high} high severity` : ''}`);
    });
    lines.push('');
  }

  for (const [system, list] of Object.entries(grouped).sort((a,b)=>b[1].length-a[1].length)) {
    const zone = getPatchZone(scriptPath, system);
    lines.push(`## System Cluster — ${system}`);
    lines.push('');
    lines.push(`Failures in cluster: ${list.length}`);
    lines.push(zone.note || '');
    if (zone.snippet) {
      lines.push('');
      lines.push('### Likely Source Area');
      lines.push('```js');
      lines.push(zone.snippet.slice(0, 4000));
      lines.push('```');
    }
    lines.push('');
  }

  for (const result of results) {
    if (result.passed && !options.includePassed) continue;
    const summary = summarizeFailure(result);
    lines.push(`## ${result.passed ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'} — ${result.name}`);
    lines.push('');
    lines.push(`Suite: ${result.suite || 'unknown'}`);
    lines.push(`Likely system: ${summary.system}`);
    if (result.maturity) lines.push(`Roadmap maturity: ${result.maturity}`);
    lines.push(`Severity: ${summary.severity}`);
    lines.push(`Confidence: ${summary.confidence}`);
    lines.push('');
    if (result.description) { lines.push('### Purpose'); lines.push(result.description); lines.push(''); }
    if (result.intendedFunction) { lines.push('### Intended function under test'); lines.push(result.intendedFunction); lines.push(''); }
    if (result.expectedOutcome) { lines.push('### Expected AI Dungeon-style outcome'); lines.push(result.expectedOutcome); lines.push(''); }
    if (result.evaluationNotes) { lines.push('### Evaluation notes'); lines.push(result.evaluationNotes); lines.push(''); }
    if (result.whyItMatters) { lines.push('### Why it matters'); lines.push(result.whyItMatters); lines.push(''); }
    if (result.steps && result.steps.length) {
      lines.push('### Minimal reproduction');
      for (const step of result.steps) lines.push(`- ${step.hook}: ${JSON.stringify(step.text || '')}`);
      lines.push('');
    }
    if (result.errors && result.errors.length) {
      lines.push('### Runtime errors');
      for (const err of result.errors) { lines.push('```text'); lines.push(String(err)); lines.push('```'); }
    }
    const failedAssertions = (result.assertions || []).filter(a => !a.passed);
    if (failedAssertions.length) {
      lines.push('### What failed');
      for (const a of failedAssertions) lines.push(assertionLine(a));
      lines.push('');
      lines.push('### What likely needs inspection');
      lines.push(result.patchHint || `Inspect ${summary.system}. The failed assertion and state diff show the expected state was not produced or exposed.`);
      lines.push('');
    }
    if (result.stateDiffs && result.stateDiffs.length) {
      lines.push('### State diffs');
      lines.push('```json');
      lines.push(JSON.stringify(result.stateDiffs.slice(0, 35), null, 2));
      lines.push('```');
      lines.push('');
    }
    if (result.debugOutputs && result.debugOutputs.length) {
      lines.push('### Debug output samples');
      for (const d of result.debugOutputs.slice(0, 3)) {
        lines.push(`#### ${d.command}`); lines.push('```text'); lines.push(String(d.text || '').slice(0, 1800)); lines.push('```');
      }
      lines.push('');
    }
  }

  const latestMd = path.join(reportDir, 'latest-report.md');
  const latestJson = path.join(reportDir, 'latest-report.json');
  const failuresJson = path.join(reportDir, 'failures-only.json');
  const aiReview = path.join(reportDir, 'ai-review-package.md');
  const patchTargets = path.join(reportDir, 'patch-targets.md');

  fs.writeFileSync(latestMd, lines.join('\n'));
  fs.writeFileSync(latestJson, JSON.stringify(results, null, 2));
  fs.writeFileSync(failuresJson, JSON.stringify(failures, null, 2));

  const patchLines = ['# Patch Targets', '', `Suite: ${options.suite || 'unknown'}`, `Failures: ${failures.length}`, ''];
  Object.entries(grouped).sort((a,b)=>b[1].length-a[1].length).forEach(([system, list], idx) => {
    const zone = getPatchZone(scriptPath, system);
    patchLines.push(`## ${idx + 1}. ${system}`);
    patchLines.push(`Failures: ${list.length}`);
    patchLines.push(zone.note || '');
    patchLines.push('Representative failures:');
    for (const f of list.slice(0, 5)) patchLines.push(`- ${f.name}`);
    if (zone.snippet) { patchLines.push('```js'); patchLines.push(zone.snippet.slice(0, 2500)); patchLines.push('```'); }
    patchLines.push('');
  });
  fs.writeFileSync(patchTargets, patchLines.join('\n'));

  const aiLines = [];
  aiLines.push('# AI Review Package');
  aiLines.push('');
  aiLines.push('Use this to ask ChatGPT for patch guidance. Focus on high severity and avoid whole-library rewrites.');
  aiLines.push('');
  aiLines.push(`Suite: ${options.suite || 'unknown'}`);
  aiLines.push(`Cases tested: ${results.length}`);
  aiLines.push(`Failures: ${failures.length}`);
  aiLines.push('');
  Object.entries(grouped).sort((a,b)=>b[1].length-a[1].length).forEach(([system, list]) => {
    aiLines.push(`## ${system} (${list.length} failures)`);
    for (const f of list.slice(0, 8)) {
      aiLines.push(`### ${f.name}`);
      if (f.description) aiLines.push(`Purpose: ${f.description}`);
      if (f.maturity) aiLines.push(`Roadmap maturity: ${f.maturity}`);
      aiLines.push('Reproduction:');
      for (const step of f.steps || []) aiLines.push(`- ${step.hook}: ${JSON.stringify(step.text || '')}`);
      aiLines.push('Failed assertions:');
      for (const a of (f.assertions || []).filter(x=>!x.passed)) aiLines.push(assertionLine(a));
      aiLines.push('');
    }
  });
  fs.writeFileSync(aiReview, aiLines.join('\n'));

  return { latestMd, latestJson, failuresJson, aiReview, patchTargets };
}

module.exports = { writeReports, likelySystemFromPath };

const fs = require('fs');
